facts.fact: 办公室门口站着 Arthur Taliesin——屋里太挤他进不来；Maggie 的脸红到了新的高度，脑子里只剩「Dr. Linden，不是 Maggie」。
facts.anchor: She turned and there was Arthur Taliesin, his eyebrows arched.

facts.fact: 贵妃榻保卫战：她拒绝撤掉沙发——它让比公寓待得还久的办公室像个家，更让学生求助时不再拘束；Taliesin 冷面追问「你在这儿经常晕倒吗」。
facts.anchor: “No, it wouldn’t. That is my fainting couch, and I won’t be getting rid of it,” she insisted.

facts.fact: 他的桌子挤在窗下、比儿童家具还小；她指着一缕阳光自称「慷慨」，他干答「Generous」——第一个冷场笑话。
facts.anchor: “See,” Maggie said, gesturing toward the sunbeam. “I’m being generous. You’re getting the only sun this room will see over the next twenty-four hours. You’re welcome.”

facts.fact: 同室办公她只撑了整整 37 分钟：翻包、批卷、抖脚，样样都是干扰；她丢下一句「出门锁门」就走。
她不敢当面质问预算被砍的事：一想到要为自己苦心经营的学术辩护就想哭；男人们怎么评价发怒落泪的女人她见识过——她拒绝在 Taliesin 面前哭。
facts.anchor: She knew from experience what men thought of women who cried out of anger.

facts.fact: 院长推牌：申请人数多年下滑后今年涨了三倍，全靠 Taliesin 镇场；Maggie 读出弦外之音——她的 tenure 悬于这位「著名酸味炼金术师」的心情。
facts.anchor: Enrollment at Hawthorn has been down for years, but this year we saw a threefold increase in applicants.

facts.fact: 她问为何不换更好的办公室：院长说 Taliesin 拒绝了 Ferox Hall 的空套间——不愿受特殊待遇，也不愿让学生多跑路；她只能挤出一句「我们会搞定的」。
facts.anchor: “He didn’t want to receive any kind of special treatment or inconvenience his students by making them walk all the way to the administration building.”

facts.fact: 结尾：院长一走，Maggie 伏案用手臂挡住光，叹了口气。
facts.anchor: When he was out of sight, Maggie put her head down on the desk, letting her arms block out the light, and sighed.
